```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's demand evidence fits the product more closely. Three independent, sourced quotes (dev.to and two Reddit threads) describe production incidents from upstream API changes, which is the exact pain the product fixes. A's two quotes are about general visibility of agent output, not about teams jointly steering or handing off agent tasks.",
    "A faces a free incumbent with wide distribution. Slack Code ships free in every Slack plan, which anchors the core feature at $0. B also has free competitors, but they are indie projects or betas, not a bundled incumbent.",
    "B has sourced paid price points that match its price hypothesis: apidrift.co at $29/mo and Nalvis at $14/mo hosted. That makes $20-50/mo plausible for a first paying customer within 90 days.",
    "B's task (watch, diff, scan, open a PR) is well bounded and can be sold self-serve through a GitHub App or the GitHub Marketplace (sourced). A's claim that it can be built solo in six weeks is marked [unsourced], so it counts as missing.",
    "A's brief itself names security and governance (SOC2, ZDR, SSO, approval gating) as the likely purchase driver for shared control over agents. That is a high bar for a solo operator before even a pilot. B shares some trust risk, but it can start with SMBs on a narrow scope.",
    "Both niches are crowded, so crowding does not separate them. The difference is that B has more specific sourced pain and a cheaper path to a small paying customer."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence does not support the product it proposes. The ops-lead quote ('What did the agents actually produce last week?') and the 'Slack turns traces into vibes' quote show a need for reporting and visibility. Neither shows anyone wanting, or paying for, multiplayer live-steering and handoff. The 'YC Fall 2026 RFS' signal cited in the Case For has no source link. The claims that demand exists beyond engineering and that the build fits in six weeks are both [unsourced].",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both ideas sit in crowded niches with free alternatives, and neither brief shows direct willingness-to-pay from a named prospect. B wins mainly on more specific, multi-source pain evidence and the lack of a free bundled incumbent. Its own risks are real and could erode that edge: false-positive trust problems (mendapi's ~8x over-reporting finding) and three competitors already offering it free. B's community-CAC figure came from a page containing a prompt-injection attempt, so it was treated as directional and given no weight."
}
```
